google.step1: In your Google Cloud project, with the Google Health API enabled, the web OAuth client must allow returning to the address below (Authorized redirect URIs). In Data access, the eight Google Health read permissions: activity, health metrics, sleep, profile, location, ECG, irregular rhythm alerts and settings.
google.step2: In Connections, Health category, connect Google Health with that client's Client ID and Client secret.
google.step3: Google asks for permission: tick every box. On returning it brings the last thirty days, and then what is new every two hours: steps, heart rate, sleep with stages, HRV, SpO₂, temperature, workouts, electrocardiograms, irregular rhythm alerts and the band battery. If you connected before ECG, alerts and settings were requested, press Reconnect in Connections.
google.step4: Before leaving the iPhone shortcut, export Apple Health and load it with scripts/apple-health-steps.py: that way the history reaches the last day.

info.afterTraining: How you slept the nights after training against the rest, over the last 90 days.
info.awakenings: The times you woke up and the time you were up, if the band gave it.

info.calendar: Each night of the month coloured by its score. Tap one to see it above.
info.dayPulse: Your heart rate today every five minutes, from the band.
info.fellAsleep: How long it took you to fall asleep: what the band says or the time awake from the start of the night to the first sleep stage, whichever is more.
info.heartTrends: The chosen figure over the last 90 days, with its 7-day average, against a month ago and your best.
info.hrv: Heart rate variability: how much the time between beats changes while you sleep, in milliseconds. Higher is usually better recovery; it is compared with you, not with others.
info.hypnogram: The night from left to right and which stage you were in: awake on top, then REM (when you dream), light and deep at the bottom. The grey line is your heart rate.
info.inBed: From when you fell asleep to when you got up, according to the band.
info.ldl: The LDL cholesterol of your last lab test and its change since the previous one.
info.load: Each training minute counts as much as its heart rate zone, from 1 to 5 (Edwards), and the week adds up. It is compared with your average of the four weeks before.
info.loadWeeks: The load of each of the last 12 weeks, Monday to Sunday.
info.naps: What you slept that day outside the main night.
info.normal: Your normal is the average of your previous 60 days ± how much you usually move (one standard deviation). Without 14 days of data there is no comparison.
info.pulseNow: The last heart rate that arrived today, in beats per minute, and when it was measured.
info.readiness: How you start the day, from 0 to 100: last night's HRV and your resting HR against your normal. 50 is the usual; more, better recovered; less, worse. It needs 14 days of HRV from the band.
info.regularity: What time you fall asleep and wake up on average over 30 nights, and how much it varies (±).
info.respiration: Breaths per minute while you sleep.
info.restingHeart: The beats per minute at rest the band works out each day, mostly while sleeping. Going down over time usually goes with getting fit.
info.schedule: From what time to what time you slept the last 14 nights, with their quality colour. Aligned bars are a regular schedule.
info.skinTemp: How far your skin temperature at night is from your usual, in degrees.
info.sleepMinutes: What you slept last night, not counting the time awake in bed, against your 60-day normal.
info.sleepScore: Last night's score, from 0 to 100: duration against 8 h (up to 50), how much was deep or REM (up to 25) and how little you were awake in bed (up to 25). 90 or more is excellent; 80, good; 60, fair.
info.spo2: Blood oxygen saturation while you sleep, as a percentage.
info.stages: How the night was split: deep is the one that restores the body most, REM the one of dreams, light the rest. Below, your average of the 30 nights before.
info.stagesTrend: The hours in each stage over the last 30 nights.
info.steps: The steps the band counts today, since 00:00. The ring fills with your steps goal (in Settings) or, without it, with your 30-day average.
info.steps7: The average steps of the seven days before today, against your goal.
info.tension: The minutes of each hour you were still and awake with your heart rate clearly above your resting. It is an estimate: coffee, heat or digestion raise it too.
info.trainingTime: The time trained from Monday to today, against your average of the four weeks before.
info.trend: The score of each night of the last 90 days with its 7-night average. The green band is good or better.
info.weight: Your weight: the average of the last 7 days and how much it changed in 30.
info.workoutsWeek: How many workouts (Training sessions and activities) you have done from Monday to today.
info.year: Each night of the year, the good or better ones in green.
info.zoneWeeks: The minutes you spent in each heart rate zone each week, adding up every workout.

shortcut.more: What else the shortcut can send
shortcut.step1: In Connections, Health category, connect Apple Health and copy the token: it is only shown that once.
shortcut.step2: On the iPhone, open Shortcuts → Automation → New, choose Time of Day, 23:30, daily, and let it run without asking.
shortcut.step3: Add Find Health Samples: type Steps, start date in the last 7 days, one more filter Source contains Watch, grouped by hour and without limit. That way, if the shortcut does not run one day, the next one picks it up.
shortcut.step4: On them, Get Details of Health Samples → Start Date, and Format Date in ISO 8601 with the time. And again Get Details of Health Samples → Value.
shortcut.step5: Repeat the two previous steps with Source does not contain Watch: the iPhone and any other app.
shortcut.step6: Add Get Contents of URL with the address below, method POST, an Authorization header with Bearer, a space and the token, and a JSON body with four text fields: watch_start and watch_steps (the Watch hours and values), and phone_start and phone_steps (the rest). Each hour counts the source that saw the most steps, as Health does: without separating them, a walk seen by the iPhone and the Watch at once counted twice.
shortcut.step7: For the rest (heart, calories, distance…), before Get Contents of URL: for each row of the list below, Find Health Samples of that type with start date today and Calculate Statistics with the calculation it says. Each result goes into the JSON body with its key, and counts for the most recent day. Leave out the ones you do not use: none is required.
shortcut.step8: If a day arrives twice, the last one wins: at 23:30 today what was sent yesterday is corrected.
